subject: Architecture
title: The Roman Aqueduct System
description: Learn The Roman Aqueduct System in one minute.

hook.text: Rome's aqueducts delivered 300 million gallons of fresh water daily — more than many modern cities manage.

buildup.text: Eleven aqueducts spanning 260 miles brought mountain water to a city of one million people.

discovery.text: Water flowed by gravity alone on a carefully calculated slope — about one foot per 300 feet of length.

twist.text: Most of the system was underground. The famous arched bridges are only a small visible fraction.

climax.text: The Pont du Gard in France still stands after 2,000 years — its arches perfect without any mortar.

punchline.text: No pumps, no electricity, no pipes. Just gravity and geometry.

quiz.question: What powered Roman aqueducts to move water?
options: Gravity on a carefully calculated slope
